messages:
charlie_customer: Hey @support — our /call to pdf_extractor is returning 400 "Failed to parse tool args: invalid JSON" after customers paste Windows paths. Repro below.

charlie_customer:
```json
{
  "tool": "pdf_extractor",
  "args": {
    "path": "C:\\Users\\charlie\\docs\\report.pdf",
    "options": { "pages": [1,2], },
  }
}
```

alice_support: Can you paste the raw request body (exact bytes the server received) and the Content-Type header?

charlie_customer: From the client clipboard -> we run a curl with single quotes and --data-binary $PASTE. $PASTE contained:

{"tool":"pdf_extractor","args":{"path":"C:\\Users\\charlie\\docs\\report.pdf","options":{"pages":[1,2],},},}

Server response: HTTP 400
body: "Failed to parse tool args: invalid JSON at position 88"

bob_engineer: Reproduced locally. The error is due to trailing commas and unescaped backslashes. The strict JSON parser fails. Quick repro (valid JSON form):

curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/call \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"tool":"pdf_extractor","args":{"path":"C:\\Users\\charlie\\docs\\report.pdf","options":{"pages":[1,2]}}}'

alice_support: Workaround for the customer: ask them to sanitize clipboard before sending. In PowerShell:

$body = '{"tool":"pdf_extractor","args":{"path":"C:\\\\Users\\\\charlie\\\\docs\\\\report.pdf","options":{"pages":[1,2]}}}'
Invoke-RestMethod -Uri 'https://api.redwood.ai/v1/call' -Method Post -Body $body -Headers @{ 'Content-Type' = 'application/json'; 'Authorization' = 'Bearer ...' }

Also recommend using forward slashes in paths or running JSON.stringify on client.

bob_engineer: Escalating to eng-runtime for improved error message + input sanitization. Created ticket INC-4821 and assigned to @bob_engineer. Plan: detect trailing commas and provide actionable error referencing offending char index, and optionally accept JSON5-ish inputs for tool args with a warning. :eyes: :hammer:

alice_support: Sent workaround to customer and flagged support ticket. Closing here once ENG confirms patch. :white_check_mark:
